target_customer: Makers of embedded vision devices such as body worn cameras, DVRs, drones, security cameras and AR hardware
problem: Embedded computer vision needs very low power silicon. REM built asynchronous resilient chips with a custom neural network architecture, claiming 3 to 4 times better energy efficiency.
business_model: Semiconductor design and chip or IP sales
product_category: Low power AI and vision chips

founders.name: Eleazar Vega-Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC as eleazar. Later built Coil (W23) per his YC bio.

founders.name: Dylan Hand
education: USC Viterbi, Ph.D. student under Peter Beerel

founders.name: William Koven
founders.background_notes: Worked with Prof. Peter Beerel at Intel per USC Viterbi Magazine.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as inactive. No shutdown notice or acquisition found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Asynchronous resilient chip design plus a custom neural network accelerator requires specialist silicon expertise, EDA tools and fabrication, which is research grade for a team of two or three.

defensibility.rationale: Asynchronous design know how was rare because incumbents had largely moved away from it, but the claim was unproven without silicon.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in 2017 framed Intel and ARM as the giants REM pitted itself against. No source shows them acting against REM.

market_need_then: Demand for low power vision in body cameras, drones and security cameras was a stated target. The 2017 TechCrunch article reported the chip design was largely complete with prototypes expected later that year.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a few press mentions, mostly one TechCrunch piece. No brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: REM came out of USC research on asynchronous chips and went through YC S15, then raised a 2 million dollar seed from Draper Associates reported in March 2017. It later joined a GlobalFoundries program to bring RISC-V IP to 22FDX. YC lists it as inactive but no cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned. A chip startup needs far more capital than a seed to reach silicon, which is context only and not a sourced cause.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 and was not read. The 2 million seed is stated by TechCrunch (opened) and a database total of 2.1M appears in search results, which is consistent; Seedtable shows no rounds. The YC 120K for 7 percent is from USC Viterbi Magazine (Spring 2016 issue, undated article). The Draper seed month is the article date and the true close date is unknown. Competitors from 2017 coverage are outside the batch window, so the list is empty and the Intel and ARM framing is only recorded under takeover risk. The GlobalFoundries program item is from a search listing, not opened, and its date is unknown. Cause of inactivity not public.
